title: Advanced TypeScript Patterns
tagline: Design types that catch real bugs, and keep them readable enough that your team still trusts them.
description: You already write TypeScript: interfaces, unions, a few generics. This course is about the next step, using the type system as a design tool. You will model domain states so impossible ones cannot be written, steer generic inference instead of fighting it, and write type-level code (mapped, conditional and template literal types) that your teammates can still read.

Every lesson builds the type layer of Cartwheel's checkout API client: money that cannot mix currencies, order statuses the compiler checks exhaustively, a fetch client typed from a route map, and parsers that turn untrusted JSON into trusted types. You finish with the parts that ship: strict tsconfig flags, declaration files, explicit resource management, decorators, and a plan for migrating a JavaScript codebase.
audience: Developers who use TypeScript every day and want types that prevent bugs instead of types that only describe code.
prerequisites: Comfortable with modern JavaScript and everyday TypeScript: annotations, interfaces, unions and basic generics.
learnItems: Model domain states with discriminated unions and literal types
Design generic APIs that infer the right types without annotations
Write mapped, conditional and template literal types with restraint
Brand IDs and money, and make switch statements exhaustive
Parse untrusted data into trusted types at the boundary
Ship strict tsconfigs, declaration files and incremental migrations
